title: Grammar-Growing Certificates — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Can a proof system safely grow its own language — letting descendants introduce new predicates, types, or inference rules — while provably preserving the meaning of everything already said? Formally, each inventive extension must carry a translation demonstrating that no claim in the old vocabulary acquires a proof it did not already have.
status: The missing ingredient is an efficient extension-certificate language that permits useful invention while excluding disguised new axioms; the proposal draws on proof-carrying data and foundational approaches to proof-carrying code.
solved_when: An extension-certificate language exists that permits useful invention of new predicates, types, and inference rules while excluding disguised new axioms, with each extension accompanied by a checkable translation certificate for conservative extension over the old vocabulary.
why: It would let verification ecosystems invent domain-specific concepts on the fly without periodically replacing their foundational trust base.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and foundational approaches to proof-carrying code.

title: Theorem-Compiler Seeds — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Can a certified theorem family carry within it a "seed" that, when developed, yields a new descendant prover and verifier whose accepted outputs stay confined to that family's authorized consequences?
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists. The surrounding state of the art rests on SuperNova's nonuniform incremental verification and CompCert's semantic-preservation methodology, which together suggest that specialization can preserve soundness while allowing cost to follow the specialized computation rather than the entire original interpreter.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a seed extracted from a certified theorem family produces a descendant prover and verifier whose accepted outputs remain inside that family's authorized consequences, with specialization preserving soundness while allowing cost to follow the specialized computation rather than the entire original interpreter.
why: It would let research programs manufacture increasingly efficient verification machinery as their theories develop, instead of paying the cost of a general interpreter for every specialized proof.
key_works: SuperNova’s nonuniform incremental verification and CompCert’s semantic-preservation methodology.

title: Challenge-Morphing Proofs — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Can a single committed object support an interactive proof system in which an adversarial verifier adaptively requests certificates of ever-stronger properties, with every response remaining jointly consistent with the same object while leaking nothing about unrequested properties? The goal is compact, adaptively secure consistency across changing relations, handling selective abort and correlated disclosures.
status: This is a proposal-stage target with no known construction; the desired features are compact, adaptively secure consistency across changing relations, including selective abort and correlated disclosures. Related machinery appears in the literature on function-hiding functional commitments.
solved_when: A construction exists for one committed object in which each adaptively requested response is jointly consistent with that object, hides all unrequested properties, and remains compact; the security proof must handle an adversarial verifier making adaptive queries, including selective abort and correlated disclosures.
why: It would enable interactive audits that deepen organically as new questions arise, instead of forcing a complete specification of all desired properties before the first certificate is issued.
key_works: Function-hiding functional commitments.

title: Latent Lemma Pods — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Build a "latent lemma pod" — a certificate that carries a hidden lemma together with its derivation and an activation predicate, such that awakening the pod discloses only the authorized lemma and carries a proof connecting it to the original theorem.
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The stated design constraints are that adaptive activation must not leak dormant lemmas through rejection behavior and must not permit stale evidence to awaken them. The suggested technical starting points are functional encryption and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A construction exists where (i) dormant pods reveal nothing about their lemmas, including through the adaptive activation mechanism's rejection behavior; (ii) stale evidence cannot awaken a pod; and (iii) upon activation, the released lemma is accompanied by a verifiable derivation and a proof tying it to the original theorem.
why: It would let scientific and institutional certificates disclose deeper justification only when warranted — during disputes, emergencies, or later research — without pre-committing the full reasoning to the public.
key_works: Functional encryption and proof-carrying data.

title: Proof-Generated Witness Markets — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Can we design a market in which a parent proof emits subproblems, acceptance relations, and escrowed rewards, together with a certificate guaranteeing that accepted solutions actually discharge the parent's specified obligations?
status: This is a proposal with no existing theory; the missing pieces are mechanisms preventing circular rewards, duplicated obligations, and generators that manufacture easy but irrelevant work. Related foundations are proof-carrying data and Zerocash-style private value conservation.
solved_when: A formal framework exists in which the emitted certificates provably prevent circular rewards, duplicated obligations, and generators that manufacture easy but irrelevant work.
why: It would enable autonomous theorem-proving, audit, and scientific-discovery economies in which useful results generate their own next-stage demand.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and Zerocash-style private value conservation.

title: Ancestry-Oblivious Proof Growth — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Histories with identical declared outputs and identical leakage must remain indistinguishable — even when they differ in branching, merging, rejected attempts, and internal participants?
status: Hiding proof contents alone is known to be insufficient; proof size, update timing, and graph access patterns also require treatment. Related tools include dynamic ZK accumulators and Path ORAM.
solved_when: A construction is given in which histories with identical declared outputs and leakage are indistinguishable across all variation in branching, merging, rejected attempts, and internal participants.
why: It would let private research organizations and negotiation networks reveal conclusions without exposing their internal structure.
key_works: Dynamic ZK accumulators and Path ORAM.

title: Semantic Proof Pruning — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: Can we design a pruning step that replaces a proof history \(H\) with a summary \(S\), together with a verifiable certificate that every query in an admitted class returns the same answer on \(H\) and on \(S\)?
status: Useful query-preserving summaries are domain-specific; arbitrary unforeseen questions cannot be supported by magical lossless compression. Key works include functional commitments and provenance algebra.
solved_when: A construction is given that, for a specified class of admissible queries, produces a summary \(S\) and a checkable certificate guaranteeing answer-equivalence of \(H\) and \(S\) on that class.
why: It would enable long-lived proof organisms whose storage does not grow in proportion to every event they have experienced.
key_works: Functional commitments and provenance algebra.

title: Coinductive Service Oaths — proposal
subfield: Proof embryology: certificates that develop new expressive power
open: How can a service prove, once and for all, that it will keep honoring its promises in perpetuity? The goal is a coinductive proof package — an invariant together with a progress argument — that establishes ongoing obligations under explicit scheduling, funding, and availability assumptions.
status: It is currently understood that a finite execution proof cannot establish unconditional future service; no such package exists yet, and the missing piece must expose and preserve the service's environmental assumptions. Related foundations come from concurrent program logics and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A certificate is produced that carries an invariant and a progress argument establishing continued operation of the service, with its environmental assumptions (scheduling, funding, availability) explicitly exposed and preserved throughout the proof.
why: It would enable persistent autonomous services whose guarantees concern continued operation rather than merely correct isolated responses, since a finite execution proof can never establish unconditional future service on its own.
key_works: Concurrent program logics and proof-carrying data.

title: Autocatalytic Patch Vaults — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can a lineage of programs carry out self-modification in the open without leaking its secrets — so that a hostile host inspecting each successive executable can verify a committed internal mutation process obeyed inherited behavior and disclosure constraints?
status: The missing theorem concerns adaptive, correlated generations — not merely the security of one obfuscated program. The proposal builds on directions such as *Cryptography with Updates* and iO constructions.
solved_when: A construction (or proof of impossibility) exists for autocatalytic patch vaults: each accepted successor executable must carry a proof that its internal mutation process respected the inherited behavior and disclosure constraints, robust against an adaptive host observing correlated generations, not just a single obfuscated program.
why: It would enable confidential autonomous software that improves itself over time without exposing its source to any maintainer.
key_works: *Cryptography with Updates* and iO constructions.

title: Patch-Existence Hiding — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can a program update mechanism be built so that a real update and a certified dummy update are computationally indistinguishable whenever their permitted observable behavior and declared resource leakage agree?
status: This is a proposal; the record states that update privacy must cover binary structure, traffic, runtime, and state migration — not just encrypted patch bytes. Related directions include updatable randomized encodings and update-hiding accumulators.
solved_when: A construction exists in which real updates and certified dummy updates with matching permitted observables and declared resource leakage are indistinguishable across binary structure, traffic, runtime, and state migration.
why: It enables maintenance that does not advertise vulnerability discoveries, internal experiments, or strategic changes.
key_works: Updatable randomized encodings and update-hiding accumulators.

title: Sealed-Patch Courtship — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can a set of contributors each submit a concealed program transformation, and a committed selection mechanism then choose and apply an admissible winning patch, without ever revealing the losing patches or exposing the recipient program to any party? In other words, we want a "sealed-patch courtship" protocol combining function-hiding commitments with updatable cryptography so that both evaluation and selection preserve privacy end to end.
status: This is a proposal with no known construction. The central obstacle is that candidate evaluation can leak the target program, and repeated competitions can leak losing intellectual property. Relevant building blocks are updatable cryptography and function-hiding commitments.
solved_when: A protocol exists in which (i) contributors commit to their transformations without revealing them, (ii) a committed selection process identifies an admissible winner, and (iii) at no point — during candidate evaluation or across repeated competitions — is the target program or any losing patch exposed.
why: It would enable collaborative improvement markets for software that no single contributor is permitted to inspect, letting many parties improve a program while its source and the losing proposals stay secret.
key_works: Updatable cryptography and function-hiding commitments.

title: Epigenetic Interface Switching — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can a program generate new interfaces in response to environmental credentials, in a way where the credential activates a generation rule but confers no authority beyond what the program's inherited policy already allows?
status: The gap is the missing composition rule; it must constrain both newly generated interfaces and information leaked by repeated environment switching. Related machinery includes Macaroons' contextual delegation and functional encryption.
solved_when: A composition rule is exhibited that constrains both the newly generated interfaces and the information leaked by repeated environment switching, so that no authority beyond the inherited policy can be obtained through any sequence of switches.
why: It would let private software adapt its capabilities to communities, devices, and institutions without distributing unrelated versions.
key_works: Macaroons’ contextual delegation and functional encryption.

title: Causal-Delta Cloaks — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: When can two versions of a program be considered indistinguishable, if what observers learn is only the semantic change between them plus whatever leakage is explicitly permitted? A formal answer requires a related-program, multiversion security definition that ordinary indistinguishability obfuscation alone does not provide.
status: Currently only a proposal; no definition exists yet. Ordinary iO does not establish the desired indistinguishability, and the relevant background is iO and updatable cryptography.
solved_when: A security definition for causal-delta cloaks is formulated under which two old–new program pairs are indistinguishable exactly when their admitted interactions reveal the same semantic change and permitted leakage, together with a construction meeting it.
why: It would enable auditable private upgrades: an external party can inspect the externally meaningful change between versions without learning anything about the hidden repair.
key_works: iO and updatable cryptography.

title: Repair-Reproduction Firewalls — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can a population of self-repairing programs delegate work to freshly generated helpers without those helpers ever accumulating more authority than they were given — even when helpers collude, share secrets, or act through their semantic effects rather than their interfaces? In other words, is there a scheme in which every generated helper receives a capability derived from its task and bound to a checked task contract, such that no coalition of helpers can reconstruct authority beyond what was delegated to it?
status: This is a proposal with no construction yet; the existing primitives it builds on are Macaroons (for derived, attenuable credentials) and proof-carrying code (for checked task contracts). The open technical gap is that attenuation must compose across helper interactions, shared secrets, and semantic effects — not merely individual API permissions.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which every generated helper receives a derived capability together with a checked task contract, and it is shown that helpers — even colluding, sharing secrets, or composing semantic effects — cannot reconstruct broader authority; attenuation must demonstrably compose across helper interactions, shared secrets, and semantic effects, not merely individual API permissions.
why: Without composable attenuation, any software population that spawns its own repair helpers risks creating an expanding administrator class, since each generation of delegation could leak authority; with it, self-maintaining software populations can delegate deeply while authority provably only ever narrows.
key_works: Macaroons and proof-carrying code.

title: Key-Reborn Successors — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: After a certified refresh that incorporates enough genuinely fresh entropy, can it be shown that an adversary holding the complete pre-refresh program state learns nothing about the successor program's protected future secrets?
status: The required theorem must combine compromise recovery with hidden program evolution and inherited capabilities; related work exists in dynamic proactive secret sharing.
solved_when: A theorem is established showing that possession of all pre-refresh state does not reveal the successor's protected future secrets, for any refresh that is certified and uses sufficient honest fresh entropy, combining compromise recovery with hidden program evolution and inherited capabilities.
why: It would give autonomous recovery that actually changes the security future of a compromised program rather than merely replacing vulnerable code.
key_works: Dynamic proactive secret sharing.

title: Quarantined Mutation Chambers — proposal
subfield: Concealed mutation: programs that generate and hide their own repairs
open: Can we construct an execution environment — a "sealed chamber" — in which candidate self-modifications run and report out only through a fixed disclosure policy, so that even the observable outputs of failed experiments leak no secrets? The goal is a chamber whose every externally visible signal, including failed tests and rejection decisions, satisfies adaptive leakage bounds.
status: Currently a proposal. The known obstruction is that even a score or acceptance bit can encode secrets, so the chamber needs adaptive leakage bounds; relevant machinery includes FHE and fully adaptive privacy composition.
solved_when: A chamber construction exists whose outputs follow a fixed disclosure policy covering failed tests and rejection decisions, and for which adaptive leakage bounds hold — no observable output (including any score or acceptance bit) encodes more than the policy permits.
why: It would let programs explore self-modification and generate their own repairs without every experimental patch being treated as trusted production code.
key_works: FHE and fully adaptive privacy composition.

title: Polycentric Organisms — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can a "polycentric" cryptographic organism be built, in which no single party or key holds full control, different committees govern distinct secret states and capabilities, and organism-level actions are only possible through certified coordination among the relevant organs?
status: Currently only a proposal; organ replacement and cross-organ failures are identified as needing a composition theorem that does not secretly reintroduce a universal recovery key. Related foundations are universally composable protocols and dynamic secret sharing.
solved_when: A construction exists with committee-controlled secret states, per-capability governance, and a composition theorem for organ replacement and cross-organ failures that provably does not reintroduce a universal recovery key.
why: It would enable autonomous entities whose internal checks and balances remain enforceable after deployment, rather than collapsing at the first coalition or organ failure.
key_works: Universally composable protocols and dynamic secret sharing.

title: Ontogenetic Quorums — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can a cryptographic organism be born with a small founding committee and then grow — its quorum sizes, access structure, and recovery rules changing through development — without ever breaking the adversary model it was certified under? Formally, the question is how to design certified ontogenetic transitions that preserve a declared adversary threshold and corruption budget across generations of the committee.
status: A proposal only; no construction exists. The core unresolved modeling issue is that adding identities does not prove additional honesty, so the model must specify enrollment assumptions and cross-generation corruption limits. Related prior work is dynamic-committee proactive secret sharing.
solved_when: A construction exists in which committee size, access structure, and recovery rules evolve through certified transitions, each provably preserving the declared adversary model, including explicit enrollment assumptions and cross-generation corruption limits.
why: It would let small organisms grow into large distributed institutions without replacing their identity or losing their secrets.
key_works: Dynamic-committee proactive secret sharing.

title: Wound-Limited Regeneration — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can a compromised cryptographic organism be brought back to health rather than restarted? A recovery should identify which compartments were compromised, revoke their future authority, and certify which unaffected state and guarantees remain valid.
status: Recovery must account for secrets already learned and capabilities already exercised, since regeneration cannot undo those facts. Related foundations come from proactive sharing and composable security models.
solved_when: A recovery mechanism exists that, after compromise, identifies the affected compartments, revokes their authority, and produces a certification of the state and guarantees that remain valid — without restarting the organism from scratch or ignoring the compromise.
why: It enables recoverable autonomous systems that neither restart from nothing nor pretend the compromise never occurred.
key_works: Proactive sharing and composable security models.

title: Metamorphic Selfhood — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: When can a cryptographic agent be said to remain itself as it changes — can identity continuity be captured as a certified relation over selected obligations and state projections, rather than mere equality of keys or program binaries?
status: This is a proposal stage problem; no construction or proof exists yet. The suggested technical grounding is proof-carrying data and contextual refinement methods.
solved_when: A formal identity relation is specified that is explicit enough to prevent arbitrary replacement of the agent while still permitting meaningful transformation, together with a certification mechanism showing when the relation holds.
why: It would let persistent agents and institutions genuinely transform over time without abandoning accountability for their prior obligations.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and contextual refinement methods.

title: Senescence Without Sovereigns — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can cryptographic capabilities be made to decay across authenticated epochs unless a precommitted renewal condition is satisfied, with that same renewal restriction inherited by every descendant? In other words, is there a formal scheme in which authority naturally ages and dies unless affirmatively renewed, so that no party can keep it alive through inertia alone?
status: The open modeling requirement is that epoch availability, emergency operation, and renewal evidence must all be modeled without granting an unrestricted override; contextual capability restrictions and cryptographic timestamping are the relevant key works.
solved_when: A formal model exists in which epoch availability, emergency operation, and renewal evidence are all handled without granting any unrestricted override — that is, the renewal and inheritance rules are specified and proved consistent with the decay and inheritance conditions across authenticated epochs.
why: It would give delegations that cannot become permanent merely through controller inertia, forcing authority to be actively re-earned rather than passively retained.
key_works: Contextual capability restrictions and cryptographic timestamping.

title: Sterile-but-Living Programs — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can a self-reproducing program be rendered permanently sterile — stripped of every capability by which it could produce new certified descendants — while its other specified execution rights are left intact, so that existing copies keep running but can never spawn fresh ones?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The requirement identified is that every recognized reproduction route, including delegation and migration, must honor the sterilization boundary. Related ideas appear in work on private spend prevention and attenuated authorization.
solved_when: A sterilization mechanism exists such that every recognized reproduction route, including delegation and migration, honors the sterilization boundary, and existing copies retain their specified execution rights but cannot obtain new certified descendants.
why: It would allow controlled deployment of useful self-reproducing systems without requiring their destruction.
key_works: Private spend prevention and attenuated authorization.

title: Cryptographic Organ Donation — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can a donor organism cryptographically delegate or transfer a specified functional capability to a recipient organism, together with explicit rules determining whether the donor's own corresponding authority survives the transfer?
status: This is a proposal with no known construction; the security requirement identified is that functional inheritance must remain secure under donor–recipient collusion and repeated extraction of overlapping "organs." Related machinery includes functional and mergeable functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which functional inheritance remains secure under donor–recipient collusion and under repeated extraction of overlapping "organs."
why: It would let private expertise, archives, and service modules be reused across independently governed organisms rather than locked to a single body.
key_works: Functional and mergeable functional encryption.

title: Posthumous Duty Engines — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic organisms: bodies, development, injury, sterility, death
open: Can we construct a "posthumous duty engine" — a mechanism whereby an organism's death disables its general capacity to act, yet activates a finite executor authorized solely to discharge obligations the organism committed to before death, using only resources reserved for that purpose?
status: This is a proposal with no construction yet. The key stated requirement is that the executor must not become a disguised continuation of the deceased organism's unrestricted authority; related foundations lie in capability attenuation and resource-accounting program logics.
solved_when: A construction exists in which death provably extinguishes the organism's general action authority while the executor (i) can complete only the finite set of pre-committed obligations, (ii) draws exclusively on reserved resources, and (iii) cannot be leveraged as a disguised continuation of the deceased organism's unrestricted authority.
why: It enables autonomous systems that can terminate without abandoning customers, counterparties, or shared infrastructure that depended on their commitments.
key_works: Capability attenuation and resource-accounting program logics.

title: Proof-Carrying Semantic Deltas — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a software patch carry a machine-checkable certificate that specifies exactly where the old and new versions' behavior may differ, and proves preservation everywhere else under an explicit execution model?
status: This is a proposal; the efficiency target stated is proof generation proportional to the affected dependency region, not the whole application. Key works mentioned as context are CompCert and ReLoC.
solved_when: A construction exists in which proof generation cost is proportional to the affected dependency region rather than the whole application, with the certificate specifying the difference region and proving preservation outside it under an explicit execution model.
why: It makes upgrades auditable as deltas against the previous version, instead of requiring the entire application to be re-audited from scratch at every change.
key_works: CompCert and ReLoC.

title: Rollback Without Resurrection — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a system be rolled back to a prior state without undoing — or accidentally replaying — effects that have already left it? Formally, a rollback must preserve a monotone external-effect history while restoring only reversible state, and every action resumed after recovery must be checked against that history.
status: Currently a proposal, with no construction or proof in place; the design point builds on RIFL's exactly-once RPC machinery and private spend prevention, and assumes participating external services expose durable admission and completion semantics.
solved_when: A rollback mechanism exists that restores only reversible state, keeps the external-effect history monotone (no resurrection of undone effects), and validates every resumed action against that history; participating external services must expose durable admission and completion semantics.
why: It gives safe recovery for autonomous agents that have already sent messages, moved resources, or changed external systems — exactly the setting where naive rollback would double-spend or resend.
key_works: RIFL’s exactly-once RPC machinery and private spend prevention.

title: Live-Upgrade Bisimulation — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a software system be upgraded while it runs — old and new code executing side by side — in a way that provably preserves its intended behavior? Formally, must every mixed-version execution, including concurrent requests and partially migrated state, simulate some admitted abstract service?
status: This is a proposal; no solution is known. The hard case is interference between old readers, new writers, and operations already in flight. The natural technical foundation is Iris and ReLoC's concurrent refinement reasoning.
solved_when: A proof (e.g., via concurrent refinement reasoning in the style of Iris/ReLoC) that all mixed-version executions, with concurrent requests and partially migrated state, simulate an admitted abstract service, including the hard case of interference between old readers, new writers, and in-flight operations.
why: It would enable continuous evolution of running software without global shutdowns and without trusting ad hoc compatibility logic between versions.
key_works: Iris and ReLoC’s concurrent refinement reasoning.

title: Contract-Discovering Descendants — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a program's descendants discover, check, and then adopt the contracts their ancestors were only assumed to satisfy, so that an inferred contract becomes authoritative only through a checked proof under the declared program semantics rather than through observation alone?
status: This is currently a proposal; no construction exists. The framing builds on proof-carrying code and foundational verification, and it is recognized that useful invariant discovery must avoid trivial guarantees and must distinguish inferred intent from proved behavior.
solved_when: A descendant system exists in which any contract inferred from observations or inheritance is promoted to an authoritative universal guarantee only after a verified proof under the declared semantics, while trivial guarantees are excluded and inferred intent is kept distinct from proved behavior.
why: It would enable software systems whose formal understanding of themselves improves after deployment, turning accumulated runtime observations into checked, trustworthy contracts.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and foundational verification.

title: Noninterfering Test Offspring — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a self-modifying software system grow its own test suite in a way that is provably free of self-serving bias — that is, can generated tests be required to follow a certified coverage generator while their oracles and protected evaluation inputs remain outside the patch's influence?
status: Currently, the information-flow requirements for test generation, oracle generation, and selection feedback are recognized as needing separate guarantees, but no unified construction is known. Related approaches draw on authenticated build processes and adaptive evaluation methods.
solved_when: A construction exists in which test generation, oracle generation, and selection feedback each carry their own information-flow guarantee, ensuring no component of the evolving patch can influence the tests, oracles, or evaluation inputs used to judge it.
why: It enables autonomous development that expands its test suite over time without the risk of rewarding tests chosen to make its own patches look good.
key_works: Authenticated build processes and adaptive evaluation methods.

title: Dependency-Boundary Shrinkage — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can a software system evolve so that each successive version replaces some of its declared trust assumptions with checked implementations or proofs, while making any newly introduced assumptions explicit? Formally, is there a notion of dependency-boundary shrinkage under which a successor's trust footprint is provably no larger—and its new assumptions are exposed—than its predecessor's?
status: A proposal only; no mechanism currently exists. Trust dependencies are understood to include compilers, deployment machinery, configuration, and external services—not only imported libraries. Related prior work includes CompCert and in-toto.
solved_when: A mechanism or framework is given in which a successor replaces specified trust assumptions (compilers, deployment machinery, configuration, external services, or imported libraries) with checked implementations or proofs, and any assumptions introduced elsewhere in the process are explicitly exposed and trackable.
why: It would let software become more independently verifiable as it evolves, rather than accumulating unverifiable trust with each change.
key_works: CompCert and in-toto.

title: Environment-True Repair Capsules — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: Can we construct repair capsules whose certificates attest to the actual environment in which a repair ran — the committed permissions, files, dependencies, pending actions, and available tools — rather than to a retrospectively cleaned view of it?
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists. Current building blocks are in-toto's process provenance and verifiable stateful execution. External nondeterminism and incomplete capture mean any solution must state explicit boundaries rather than claim perfect replay.
solved_when: A capsule mechanism exists that binds each repair certificate to the concrete environment state (permissions, files, dependencies, pending actions, tools) at repair time, and gives sound, checkable boundaries for external nondeterminism and incomplete capture instead of claiming perfect replay.
why: It would make autonomous incident response credible and enable repair-learning datasets free of hidden environmental substitutions.
key_works: in-toto’s process provenance and verifiable stateful execution.

title: Protocol Molting — proposal
subfield: Proof-carrying software evolution
open: When a protocol "molts" — replacing its message formats and rules while clients of the old and new versions coexist — what single evidence must be produced so that the transition itself, not just each version in isolation, is certified secure? Formally, this asks for an accepted molt that preserves the specified guarantees across all enrolled old and new clients, including messages created before the activation of the new version but delivered afterward.
status: The state of the art does not solve this: cross-version authentication and delayed authority are not solved merely by proving each version separately. Related foundations come from composable security and relational program verification.
solved_when: A molt is accepted only when the specified guarantees are shown to hold across enrolled old and new clients, covering messages created before activation but delivered afterward.
why: It would let long-lived protocols change fundamentally without treating delayed cross-version traffic as an exceptional afterthought.
key_works: Composable security and relational program verification.

title: Optimizer-Complete Bloodlines — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can we build a training lineage in which every accepted update carries an efficiently verifiable proof that it — including weights, optimizer accumulators, data ordering, randomness, learning-rate state, and restart decisions — derives exactly from its committed parent?
status: This is a proposal; the target is an efficient proof of the complete update state, including mixed-precision and implementation-specific behavior. Key works: recursive zero-knowledge proofs of training.
solved_when: An accepted update is accompanied by an efficient proof of the complete update state, covering mixed-precision and implementation-specific behavior, with the proof binding all of the above components to the committed parent.
why: It would make fine-tuning lineages meaningful across pauses, migrations, and distributed training, where today the unproven optimizer and implementation state silently breaks provenance.
key_works: Recursive zero-knowledge proofs of training.

title: Causal Fine-Tuning Twins — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can a training pipeline produce a pair of "fine-tuning twins" — two certified runs that start from the same prescribed initialization and share the same prescribed randomness, differing only in one declared intervention such as an added dataset — so that any difference between the resulting models is attributable to that intervention?
status: This is a proposal. Such twins would establish algorithmic counterfactuals under the specified experiment, not unrestricted causal claims about real-world usefulness. Related machinery includes proofs of training and verifiable unlearning.
solved_when: A construction exists in which two training runs verifiably share their prescribed initialization and randomness while differing in exactly one declared intervention (e.g., an added dataset), with certification of this shared provenance.
why: It enables private, reproducible attribution of model changes to particular learning decisions, letting one prove which intervention caused which behavioral difference.
key_works: Proofs of training and verifiable unlearning.

title: Synthetic-Data Inheritance Rules — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can provenance and permitted-use predicates attached to synthetic training examples be made to survive arbitrary transformations, so that any enrolled descendant of the data still carries them? Formally, is there an inheritance rule under which transformations cannot strip these predicates merely by changing the data's representation?
status: The guarantee is currently known to require mediated lineage admission; cryptography cannot detect every externally reintroduced paraphrase. Related foundations include proof-carrying data and adaptive privacy composition.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which enrolled synthetic examples inherit provenance and permitted-use predicates and no transformation removes those predicates purely through change of representation, within the mediated lineage admission framework.
why: It would make consent and privacy accounting robust across model ecosystems, so that distillation and synthetic-data reuse do not automatically erase them.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and adaptive privacy composition.

title: Learner-Reachable Teaching — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can a teacher's artifact be made to carry a certified action sequence showing that a learner, starting from its committed state and using only its available tools and permissions, could in fact execute what is being taught? Formally: construct a teaching artifact whose reachability proof is checked against the learner's actual committed state, tool set, and permission set.
status: This is a proposal stage. Note that reachability alone does not prove the teacher lacked hindsight; that separate information boundary must remain explicit. Related areas are stateful verifiable computation and process provenance.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the teaching artifact includes a certified action sequence from the learner's committed state, using only the learner's available tools and permissions, and the reachability check is verifiable.
why: It enables distillation from successful repairs without teaching impossible jumps through missing files, privileges, or infrastructure.
key_works: Stateful verifiable computation and process provenance.

title: Evaluation-Quarantined Germlines — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can a lineage of self-improving models be constructed so that every descendant provably inherits only information that has been formally accounted for at each evaluation step, with scores, selection outcomes, and even rejected experiments all counted toward the budget?
status: Complete mediation of all information flows is difficult, and a newly enrolled ancestor may already contain unaccounted external information, so no construction currently achieves the property. Related groundwork comes from reusable holdouts and fully adaptive privacy accounting.
solved_when: A germline construction exists in which every descendant carries the cumulative allowed information obtained from protected evaluators — including scores, selection outcomes, and rejected experiments — with no unaccounted channel into any ancestor or descendant.
why: It would let self-improvement experiments report progress that remains interpretable across generations, instead of silently drifting through untracked leakage from the evaluators that guide selection.
key_works: Reusable holdouts and fully adaptive privacy accounting.

title: Counterfactual Erasure Branches — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can a system that generates descendants under a specified removal procedure also produce proofs that the permitted comparisons between the actual and erased branches were carried out faithfully?
status: This is a proposal; no results are yet established. The guiding caution is that correct execution of an unlearning algorithm must not be confused with a stronger distributional erasure guarantee it lacks. Key works: Cryptographically verifiable machine unlearning.
solved_when: The system constructs descendants consistent with the specified removal procedure and proves the permitted comparisons between actual and erased branches; no quantitative targets (round counts, exponents, budgets, or sizes) are stated in the record, so this qualitative criterion stands.
why: It enables auditable decisions about deletion, retention, and downstream replacement without immediately exposing or deploying every candidate.
key_works: Cryptographically verifiable machine unlearning.

title: Encrypted Skill Budding — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can a "child" model be derived from a parent model through an approved extraction or distillation procedure, given only a restricted interface and inherited disclosure constraints, in a way that provably limits what leaks about the parent beyond the approved scope?
status: This is a proposal; no construction or security definition exists yet. Behavioral specialization alone does not establish reduced information leakage; the restriction needs its own security definition. Key works: proofs of training and functional encryption.
solved_when: A formal security definition exists for the restriction inherited by the child, and a construction is shown that produces behaviorally specialized descendants whose information leakage about the parent is bounded under that definition.
why: It would enable markets for narrowly scoped machine expertise — selling or licensing a specialized skill — without transferring, or revealing, the complete parent model.
key_works: Proofs of training and functional encryption.

title: Self-Updating Inference Receipts — proposal
subfield: Learning bloodlines: models that generate accountable descendants
open: Can we design receipts that keep every response cryptographically tied to the exact sequence of inference and authorized update steps that produced it, so that no checkpoint can be silently swapped in and no hidden adaptation can occur during serving?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The main obstacle on the table is that proof cost and state synchronization must remain manageable when inference and learning interleave at fine granularity. Related directions include recursive training proofs and modular zkML proof construction.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each output carries an authenticated binding to its full lineage of inference and authorized update steps, while proof cost and state synchronization remain manageable even when inference and learning interleave at fine granularity.
why: It would make continually learning agents whose individual outputs retain inspectable lineage, so that any deviation from the authorized checkpoint or update history is detectable rather than silent.
key_works: Recursive training proofs and modular zkML proof construction.

title: Objective-Breeding Constitutions — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: How can an institution that evolves its own objective function do so only through certified transformations, without ever violating a core set of constraints anchored outside its change process?
status: This is currently only a proposal; the objective-change rules themselves still require legitimate specification, since cryptography cannot determine which values deserve protection. Related machinery includes function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A specification exists under which any new objective is accepted only if it satisfies certified transformation rules and provably preserves the separately anchored constraint set.
why: It would let institutions learn what to optimize without silently abandoning their original commitments.
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.

title: Private-Regret Mandates — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can a delegation mandate carry a certified cumulative-regret calculation over authenticated losses, measured against a preregistered comparator family, so that adaptive delegation is evaluated against explicit alternatives rather than favorable anecdotes?
status: No such package currently exists; what is missing must bind every relevant round and distinguish formal regret from real-world welfare. Related foundations include verifiable stateful computation and authenticated derived computations.
solved_when: A package exists that binds every relevant round, computes cumulative regret over authenticated losses relative to the preregistered comparator family, and distinguishes formal regret from real-world welfare.
why: It replaces evaluation by favorable anecdotes with accountable selection against explicit alternatives, enabling rules that generate rules under verifiable measurement of their own performance.
key_works: Verifiable stateful computation and authenticated derived computations.

title: Experiment-Born Charters — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can an institution be designed so that any daughter institution it spawns derives legitimate authority solely from a precommitted selection rule applied to authenticated trial evidence, while the constraints protecting participants remain inviolable throughout? In other words, when does a fixed, accountable rule for evaluating experiments suffice to authorize new rules — with no other path to institutional change?
status: The current barrier is that trial validity depends on actual enrollment and measurement assumptions, not merely on correct execution of the scoring circuit; related adaptive data-analysis methods and attenuated capabilities are cited as key works.
solved_when: A formal specification exists in which a daughter institution's authority is granted only through the precommitted selection rule applied to authenticated trial evidence, participants' constraints are provably preserved, and trial validity is shown to depend only on conditions the specification can enforce — including the underlying enrollment and measurement assumptions, not just correct execution of the scoring circuit.
why: It would allow institutions to evolve through bounded, reversible experimentation rather than irreversible system-wide replacement, making adaptation safe without gambling the whole institution on each change.
key_works: Adaptive data-analysis methods and attenuated capabilities.

title: Mutation-Proof Exit Rights — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can a governance system be designed so that no sequence of amendments, however adversarial, can ever strip members of a funded and executable exit path? Formally: under a specified failure and adversary model, every rule-change permitted by the system must preserve an exit strategy that remains funded and executable.
status: This is a proposal stage problem. It has been observed that exit guarantees must include data access, settlement, and availability, not merely an "exit" function in source code. Related directions include composable protocol guarantees and resource-sensitive verification.
solved_when: A formal rule system and adversary/failure model are given, with a proof (or verified mechanism) that every admissible amendment preserves an exit guarantee that is funded and executable — where executability includes data access, settlement, and availability, not merely an "exit" function in source code.
why: It enables deep cooperation among parties who are unwilling to trust future institutional leadership, by making exit rights mutation-proof rather than dependent on the goodwill of whoever holds amendment power.
key_works: Composable protocol guarantees and resource-sensitive verification.

title: Generation-Spanning Conflict Checks — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: A selection proof checks candidate, evaluator, and beneficiary relationships across an authenticated succession graph while concealing irrelevant identities. Can a proof system be constructed that verifies all generation-spanning conflict relations over such a graph without revealing identities not needed for the check?
status: No construction exists yet; this is a proposal. The known limitation is that the guarantee is only as complete as the enrolled control graph, since hidden real-world ownership is not cryptographically observable. Related techniques include ZK set operations and distributed graph certification.
solved_when: A construction exists that, given an authenticated succession graph, proves the absence of conflicts among candidate, evaluator, and beneficiary relationships across generations while concealing irrelevant identities, with the completeness caveat that guarantees hold only relative to the enrolled control graph.
why: It would enable private institutional experimentation — groups generating and revising their own rules under accountable selection — with auditable restrictions on self-dealing.
key_works: ZK set operations and distributed graph certification.

title: Dissent-Generating Amendments — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can an amendment to a governance protocol be required to carry, as part of its certificate, the strongest violations it causes within a committed finite objection language — or proofs that no such violations exist?
status: The objection language must be useful and explicit; completeness cannot mean "every objection anyone could imagine." Related groundwork comes from functional commitments and verifiable computation.
solved_when: An amendment certificate construction exists that either provably identifies the strongest violations of the proposal within a fixed, explicitly specified finite objection language, or proves that no violations exist in that language.
why: It would let governance proposals arrive with authenticated adversarial analysis attached, rather than selectively chosen supporting arguments.
key_works: Functional commitments and verifiable computation.

title: Private Bargain Germination — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can an evolving institution renegotiate its rules so that a new rule is adopted only when it improves or preserves every enrolled party's committed utility under the negotiated criterion, without any party's private valuation being revealed?
status: This is a proposal, not a settled line of work. Adaptive bargaining is known to leak preferences, and strategic preference reports remain an open mechanism-design issue. Related primitives come from secure computation and function-hiding commitments.
solved_when: A mechanism is specified in which acceptance of a proposed rule is decided by whether it preserves or improves every enrolled party's committed utility under the negotiated criterion, and this decision is reached without public disclosure of reservation values or preference leakage during bargaining.
why: It would let institutions repeatedly generate and revise rules under accountable selection while keeping parties' reservation values private, something current adaptive bargaining cannot do because preference leaks and strategic preference reports remain unsolved.
key_works: Secure computation and function-hiding commitments.

title: Two-Speed Constitutional Metabolism — proposal
subfield: Evolving institutions: rules that generate rules under accountable selection
open: Can an institution whose rules rewrite themselves keep its constitution genuinely off-limits to ordinary rule changes? Every mutation should be typed as operational or constitutional, with proofs that operational changes cannot simulate forbidden constitutional effects.
status: Syntactic classification is known to be insufficient — a seemingly ordinary rule can indirectly change who controls resources. Related foundations come from proof-carrying code and contextual authorization.
solved_when: A formal typing and proof system exists in which each mutation is classified as operational or constitutional, and it is verified that operational changes cannot indirectly produce any forbidden constitutional effect.
why: It would enable adaptable institutions whose rules can evolve without an emergency loophole that gradually becomes unrestricted sovereignty.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and contextual authorization.

title: Theorem-Fertile Myths — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can we design cryptographic "myths" — authenticated statements that spawn further provable statements — such that every descendant statement is derived from the parent’s canonical semantic output and a certified generator, rather than from arbitrary proof encodings a prover can manipulate?
status: The design constraint identified so far is that the generator must create meaningful obligations while preventing circular endorsement and uncontrolled assumption growth. Related machinery includes proof-carrying data and authenticated derived computation.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a certified generator produces descendant obligations that are meaningful, circular endorsement is prevented, and assumption growth remains controlled.
why: It would enable self-expanding formal traditions, simulations, and collective narratives whose claims remain cryptographically authenticatable as they propagate.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and authenticated derived computation.

title: Unpaid-Lemma Mythologies — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can we construct a formal mythology — a system in which every derived world or claim must carry an authenticated record of its undischarged assumptions — such that no transformation anywhere in the system can relabel a conditional conclusion as unconditional without the required proofs being supplied?
status: Currently a proposal, framed within cryptographic mythologies (authenticated claims that generate further worlds); the identified technical tension is that dependency compression must preserve logical obligations even when alternative derivations and shared assumptions appear. Key works: provenance semirings and ZK accumulators.
solved_when: A construction exists in which every descendant provably carries an authenticated set of undischarged assumptions, and this invariant is preserved under dependency compression, including when alternative derivations and shared assumptions appear.
why: It would give speculative scientific and cultural systems a rigorous way to distinguish fertile conjecture from established consequence, keeping provenance honest as ideas propagate and recombine.
key_works: Provenance semirings and ZK accumulators.

title: Paraconsistent Cryptographic Worlds — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can cryptographic claims be made to carry their own logical contexts, so that communities with incompatible assumptions can still compute together? The target is a world-model in which every authenticated claim is tagged with its context, and cross-context derivation proceeds only through a checked, non-explosive calculus with explicitly specified export rules.
status: The cryptography itself is viewed as the easier part; the hard research target is useful, composable context-export rules. Related enforcement of language semantics via PCD is noted as a key direction.
solved_when: A composable set of context-export rules is defined and shown to be useful, with a checked non-explosive calculus governing cross-context derivations between explicitly context-tagged claims.
why: It would enable shared computational institutions among communities whose underlying assumptions are mutually incompatible.
key_works: PCD-based enforcement of language semantics.

title: Ritual Role Genesis — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can a digital process create a new role schema together with its initial holders, so that the new role's authority provably derives only from capabilities the participants already possess?
status: No construction is known. The surrounding context is contextual credentials and authenticated process provenance; the core constraint identified is that role invention must not become authority invention — colluding participants cannot delegate powers they never possessed.
solved_when: A protocol exists that generates a role schema and its initial holders with a proof that the new role's authority follows from the participants' existing capabilities; in particular, colluding participants cannot delegate powers they never possessed.
why: It would let communities invent offices, memberships, and shared responsibilities without relying on a permanent central registrar, while preventing role invention from becoming authority invention.
key_works: Contextual credentials and authenticated process provenance.

title: Metaphor Transport Proofs — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: When a claim carries structural predicates—dependency, obligation, role correspondence—across a translation, can we build a transformation that preserves exactly those declared predicates while explicitly flagging any interpretation that goes beyond them? In other words, a "metaphor transport" that is provably faithful to the structure it asserts and honest about the semantics it cannot vouch for.
status: Human meaning is acknowledged to exceed the formal predicates, and the requirement is that the certificate make that boundary visible; related machinery is expected from homomorphic signatures and provenance algebra.
solved_when: A formal transformation exists, with proof, that preserves every declared structural predicate under transport and produces a certificate labeling each unsupported semantic interpretation—making the boundary between the formal and the human meaning explicit and checkable.
why: It would allow claims to travel between cultural, institutional, and machine-readable worlds without falsely claiming universal semantic equivalence; without such a bound, every translation silently overstates what it guarantees.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures and provenance algebra.

title: Secret-Origin Canons — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can we construct a system of "secret-origin canons" — authenticated generative records — in which every canonical descendant carries a proof that it descends from an authorized root set and obeys the inheritance rules, while disclosing only selected origin predicates? The informal goal is ancestry that is provable yet selectively revealing: a verifier learns compliance and descent, not the full lineage.
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists in the record. The identified obstacle is that repeated ancestry queries can jointly reveal origins, especially when descendants merge. Related machinery is ZK accumulators and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each canonical descendant produces a zk-style proof of (i) ancestry from the authorized root set and (ii) compliance with the inheritance rules, revealing at most the designated origin predicates — and, given the threat noted in the record, repeated ancestry queries (particularly for descendants that merge multiple lineages) do not jointly reveal origins beyond the selected predicates.
why: It would allow durable generative traditions to persist with verifiable lineage even when their founders must remain unexposed, protecting vulnerable origins without sacrificing authenticity.
key_works: ZK accumulators and proof-carrying data.

title: Canonical Miracle Generators — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can we construct a system in which a precommitted stochastic process, together with a rarity predicate fixed in advance, determines which events count as "miracles," and every admitted event carries a proof of its position in the enrolled sampling history?
status: No construction exists; currently, hidden reruns and selective abort can manufacture apparent miracles unless enrollment and randomness are controlled. Related building blocks are functional commitments and cryptographic timestamping.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the sampling process and rarity predicate are precommitted, all sampling runs are enrolled (no hidden reruns or selective abort), and each admitted event yields a verifiable proof of its position in the enrolled history.
why: It would make verifiable surprise itself a generative ingredient, with concrete applications to games, ceremonies, science, and collective storytelling.
key_works: Functional commitments and cryptographic timestamping.

title: Hereditary Interpretation Windows — proposal
subfield: Cryptographic myths: authenticated claims that generate further worlds
open: Can a cryptographic scheme let an author commit to content together with an interpretation grammar, so that later descendants can produce new formal readings of that content only when accompanied by certificates of admissibility? Formally, this asks for a commitment mechanism whose derived readings are authenticated against the grammar, not merely against the original signature.
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The key requirement is that the interpretation grammar must constrain semantic use, not merely accept any syntactic paraphrase. Related primitives are homomorphic signatures and function-hiding commitments.
solved_when: A construction exists in which an author commits to content and an interpretation grammar, descendants can derive new formal readings only with admissibility certificates, and the grammar constrains semantic use rather than accepting any syntactic paraphrase.
why: It would enable open-ended narratives and agreements that can be developed over time without permitting arbitrary retrospective endorsement of readings their authors never intended.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures and function-hiding commitments.

title: Causal Memorial Crystals — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can we construct a cryptographic memorial — an append-only record of events — that authenticates message-level causal ancestry and supports selective proofs of ordering, dependence, and concurrency, without revealing any unrelated events? In other words, can a prover convince a verifier of a causal relationship among recorded events while keeping the rest of the history private?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. Authenticated causal references establish recorded process dependence, not the ultimate truth of every reported event. Related directions include provenance semirings and distributed ZK graph certification.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each recorded event's causal ancestry is authenticated at the message level, and a prover can produce verifiable proofs of ordering, dependence, or concurrency for any chosen pair or subset of events, with such proofs leaking no information about events not referenced in the proof.
why: It would let archives explain how an outcome arose — proving the causal chain behind it — without publishing every participant's history, enabling accountable provenance for private distributed systems.
key_works: Provenance semirings and distributed ZK graph certification.

title: Query-Born Memories — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can we design cryptographic memories in which every derived answer automatically becomes an archive object that carries its source dependencies, its transformation rule, and its remaining disclosure restrictions?
status: This is a proposal; no construction is known. The core difficulty is that repeated reuse and recombination must account for information revealed by the entire answer family. Related tools come from provenance algebra and adaptive privacy filters.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each derived answer is itself a first-class archive object with its provenance (source dependencies, transformation rule, and disclosure restrictions) recorded and enforceable, and repeated reuse and recombination provably account for the information revealed by the entire answer family.
why: It would enable collective knowledge that grows through use without losing the distinction between original testimony and derived inference.
key_works: Provenance algebra and adaptive privacy filters.

title: Re-examinable Memory Fossils — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can we build a "memory fossil" — a small commitment to an archived corpus together with its custody guarantees — such that authenticated queries about that corpus can be answered and verified long after the fact, without the commitment itself having to store all the underlying evidence?
status: This is a proposal with no existing construction; the open problems are making long-term retrievability and future-query privacy survive custodian turnover and changing cryptographic assumptions. Related tools include compact proofs of retrievability and functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction exists in which a compact commitment to an archived corpus supports later authenticated queries, and both long-term retrievability and future-query privacy survive custodian turnover and changes in cryptographic assumptions.
why: It would yield small, portable memorials that can support investigations their first summarizers never anticipated.
key_works: Compact proofs of retrievability and functional encryption.

title: Consent-Aging Archives — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can an archive's access policy evolve over time through authenticated consent and succession rules, so that authority passes to legitimate successors even as earlier public disclosures remain permanently irreversible? In other words, is there a policy calculus in which consent chains, absent participants, and inherited authority are handled explicitly and soundly?
status: No construction exists; the current state is a proposal noting that conflicting consent, absent participants, and inherited authority demand an explicit policy calculus. Key works: functional encryption and attenuated authorization.
solved_when: A formal policy model and construction exist in which (i) policy changes require authenticated consent or valid succession, (ii) once a disclosure is public it is explicitly irreversible and no later policy change can falsify it, and (iii) conflicting consent, absent participants, and inherited authority are resolved by explicit, checkable rules.
why: It would allow archives to move between secrecy, collective use, and eventual disclosure without relying on a permanent, omnipotent custodian.
key_works: Functional encryption and attenuated authorization.

title: Memorial Recombination — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can memories held by different communities be merged into a single memorial that certifies which overlapping records were agreed to refer to the same underlying entity, while deliberately preserving — rather than erasing — claims and contradictions that are specific to individual sources? Formally, construct a merge in which the agreed identity relation between overlapping records is proved, and source-specific assertions survive the recombination intact.
status: This is a proposal stage; no construction is known. Record identity is often uncertain in practice, and approximate matching must not be silently treated as exact historical identity. Related technical machinery includes ZK authenticated set operations and provenance semirings.
solved_when: A merged memorial exists that (i) carries a proof of the agreed identity relation between overlapping records, and (ii) preserves all source-specific claims and contradictions, with approximate record matches never silently treated as exact historical identity.
why: It would let communities that cannot simply pool their archives maintain a trustworthy collective memory, avoiding both false unification of merely similar records and the loss of dissenting source-specific claims.
key_works: ZK authenticated set operations and provenance semirings.

title: Countermemory Challenges — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can a cryptographic challenge mechanism prove that authenticated evidence contradicts a specified formal claim, creating a persistent dispute object that stands until the parties reconcile or a qualified revision is made?
status: The proposal notes that the contradiction relation must be explicit, since conflicting accounts are not automatically proof that one is false. Related technical machinery includes ZK set proofs and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A challenge protocol is specified in which the contradiction relation is explicit — so that conflicting accounts alone do not constitute proof of falsity — and any successful challenge yields a persistent dispute object that persists until reconciliation or qualified revision.
why: It would enable correctable public memory without requiring whistleblowers to publish everything they know.
key_works: ZK set proofs and proof-carrying data.

title: Anonymous Ancestral Credit — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can we construct a cryptographic commitment scheme under which a fixed reward is split among the members of an admitted derivation ancestry, so that no party can present the same derivation path more than once to amplify its share?
status: This is a proposal stage problem; no construction exists. Provenance semirings and Zerocash are noted as key works. A design constraint on record: procedural contribution is not identical to intellectual authorship, so the credit rule must state what it actually measures.
solved_when: A credit rule is specified that provably conserves the total reward across all admitted ancestors, with uniqueness of derivation paths enforced so repeated claims cannot multiply entitlement.
why: It would let memory commons — shared, growing cryptographic memories — preserve attribution and compensation without exposing participants' public personal histories.
key_works: Provenance semirings and Zerocash.

title: Memory-Generated Investigations — proposal
subfield: Memorial cryptography: memories that grow without falsifying their ancestry
open: Can a generator be certified to convert its own blind spots — missing fields, contradictions, unsupported dependencies — into well-formed new evidence requests, while remaining committed to a fixed coverage policy? Formally, this asks for gap definitions and a certification mechanism whose generated investigations cannot drift toward convenient, easily answered questions.
status: The system needs nontrivial gap definitions and defenses against repeatedly investigating convenient questions; background comes from provenance analysis and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A generator exists with nontrivial definitions of gaps and defenses against repeatedly investigating convenient questions, such that every missing field, contradiction, or unsupported dependency it detects yields an evidence request consistent with the committed coverage policy.
why: It enables collective memories that actively improve rather than merely accumulate, ensuring gaps are pursued rather than left dormant or exploited.
key_works: Provenance analysis and proof-carrying data.

title: Purpose-Blind Dream Foundries — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can a group of parties jointly select, under multiparty secrecy, a hidden "purpose" program, evaluate it, and commit to its result before the purpose itself is permitted to be disclosed? Formally: is there a protocol in which evaluation and result binding both precede disclosure, so the committed result cannot depend on knowledge of the program?
status: This is a proposal with no construction; currently, runtime, circuit shape, inputs, and selective abort can reveal the purpose unless included in the leakage model. Relevant building blocks include FHE and function-hiding commitments.
solved_when: A construction is given in which a purpose program selected under multiparty secrecy is evaluated and bound to a result commitment strictly before its permitted disclosure, with runtime, circuit shape, inputs, and selective abort included in the leakage model.
why: It would enable audits and decisions that executors cannot tailor to a known purpose, removing the incentive and ability to bias outcomes once the goal is known.
key_works: FHE and function-hiding commitments.

title: Space Commitments — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can we build a commitment to an entire "question space" — a representation from which answers to a whole family of future queries can later be extracted and verified — with a precise tradeoff between preprocessing cost, representation size, and per-query work? Formally, such a commitment should bind every answer in the supported family, and the family of supported questions must be made explicit.
status: This is a proposal-stage question with no known construction; the basic obstruction is already clear, namely that arbitrary future questions cannot all receive cheap answers from a tiny representation, so the supported family must be explicit. Related machinery includes functional commitments and functional encryption.
solved_when: A construction is given with an explicit supported query family and a proved tradeoff among preprocessing cost, commitment size, and query/verification work — noting that arbitrary future questions cannot all be answered cheaply from a small representation.
why: It would let scientific and institutional computation be prepared once for purposes that only emerge later, without re-running or re-committing to the data.
key_works: Functional commitments and functional encryption.

title: Encrypted Counterfactual Sleep — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can we design a protocol in which a party commits to a family of scenarios, privately evaluates all of them under encryption, and only later — once authenticated evidence arrives — selectively reveals the single outcome corresponding to the branch that actually occurred? Formally, this asks for a computation on encrypted inputs whose decryption is conditioned on a post-hoc authenticated choice, without exposing results from the unselected branches.
