status: The proposal is at the idea stage: the central obstacles identified are scenario explosion and correlations between opened branches, both of which require explicit efficiency and disclosure limits. No concrete construction is known; the suggested building blocks are FHE and recursive stateful computation.
solved_when: A protocol exists that handles a committed scenario family with explicit, proven bounds on efficiency against scenario explosion and on disclosure of correlations between opened branches, such that only the branch selected by authenticated evidence is revealed.
why: It would let contingency systems prepare results for every possible event in advance without leaking their full strategy — only the outcome that actually matters is ever disclosed.
key_works: FHE and recursive stateful computation.

title: Dream-to-Purpose Selection — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can a system, after committing to a result \(y\), derive from it a purpose \(q=G(y)\) using a generator \(G\) that was committed to in advance, and then prove both that the chronology was respected and that \(q\) was faithfully generated from \(y\)?
status: The purpose may disclose sensitive properties of \(y\), so purpose generation needs its own leakage contract. Related building blocks are function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.
solved_when: A construction exists in which, given commitments to \(y\) and a pre-committed generator \(G\), the system outputs \(q=G(y)\) together with a proof of both correct chronology (G committed before y) and faithful generation, under a stated leakage contract for the purpose itself.
why: It enables research and planning systems whose questions emerge naturally from discoveries, without any possibility of retrospective manipulation of those questions; without a leakage contract, however, the purpose itself may disclose sensitive properties of \(y\).
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and proof-carrying data.

title: Failed-Awakening Privacy — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can we design a dream protocol in which an adversary observing both accepted and rejected query transcripts learns only about a specified class of responses, with the guarantee explicitly accounting for whatever information the acceptance policy itself necessarily leaks? In other words, find a simulation-style or indistinguishability-based definition (and a construction meeting it) that treats the accept/reject bit as part of the leakage rather than ignoring it.
status: This is currently a proposal with no known construction or definition. The motivating observation is that rejection bits alone can be used to reconstruct a hidden policy or data, so any meaningful guarantee must quantify that leakage channel rather than ignore it; the natural technical toolkit is functional-encryption security definitions and adaptive privacy accounting.
solved_when: A formal definition of failed-awakening privacy exists, together with a protocol proven to satisfy it: transcripts of accepted and rejected queries reveal nothing beyond the specified response class plus a quantified bound on the acceptance channel, and that bound is integrated into the privacy accounting.
why: It would let sensitive computation safely face exploratory, future-purpose requests — users could probe whether a computation is feasible or permitted without that probing itself compromising the hidden policy or data.
key_works: Functional-encryption security definitions and adaptive privacy accounting.

title: Mutually Uninterpretable Dreams — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can a set of custodians, each holding a protected share of a computed result, later select any authorized joint purpose under which exactly the permitted function of their combined shares becomes learnable — and nothing else?
status: The proposal is framed within "results before interpretation" dream protocols; the central open requirement is adaptive collusion security, since repeated coalition changes and overlapping interpretations must be handled. A related starting point is mergeable functional encryption.
solved_when: A dream protocol exists in which custodians hold protected result shares prepared before their eventual partners or application are known, and an authorized joint purpose reveals precisely the permitted function of the combination, with adaptive collusion security against repeated coalition changes and overlapping interpretations.
why: It would enable collaborations where participants prepare useful work before knowing their eventual partners or application, instead of forcing them to fix the coalition and the interpretation upfront.
key_works: Mergeable functional encryption.

title: Delayed-Meaning Signatures — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: Can we construct a signature scheme in which statements made in the future receive valid derived signatures only when they are interpreted through an authenticated interpretation language, with context restrictions preserved across derivations?
status: This is a proposal; unrestricted derivability is known to create unintended endorsements, and it is recognized that the interpretation policy must constrain both content and context. Related background comes from homomorphic signatures.
solved_when: A scheme exists in which no valid derived signature can be produced for a future statement except via the authenticated interpretation policy, and the policy provably constrains both the content and the context of any endorsed meaning.
why: It would enable preauthorized scientific results, contingent agreements, and machine-generated attestations whose future meanings remain bounded by the signer's intent, preventing unintended endorsements.
key_works: Homomorphic signatures.

title: Dream Compost — proposal
subfield: Dream protocols: results before interpretation
open: How can a transformation harvest reusable structure from sealed cryptographic results — the "compost" of abandoned computations — without leaking anything that the original purpose was never authorized to reveal? Formally, the goal is a transformation that extracts approved reusable structure from sealed results while provably carrying forward all of their disclosure and provenance constraints.
status: The core hazard is identified: reuse can expose information that no original purpose was permitted to reveal, so permissions must compose across transformation chains. Related primitives include FHE, functional encryption, and adaptive privacy filters, but no construction meeting the goal is known.
solved_when: A transformation mechanism exists that extracts approved reusable structure from sealed results and composes permissions correctly across chains of such transformations, so that nothing becomes visible through reuse that the original disclosure constraints forbade.
why: It would enable economies of reusable private precomputation and let research compound across abandoned purposes, rather than discarding sealed results entirely.
key_works: FHE, functional encryption, and adaptive privacy filters.

title: Proof-Certified Tissues — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can a growing authenticated network admit new nodes and edges only when they carry locally verifiable evidence that the enlarged graph still satisfies chosen connectivity, separation, or resource invariants — so that correctness of the tissue's global structure is maintained through growth itself?
status: This is a proposal-stage research target; the emphasis is on local update cost and privacy across growth, not merely proving a static graph property. Related key works concern distributed noninteractive zero-knowledge proofs.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each admitted node or edge carries evidence that the enlarged authenticated graph satisfies the selected invariants, with the update and verification cost local rather than requiring a trusted observer of the whole network; privacy of the growth process is preserved across updates.
why: It would enable self-assembling distributed infrastructure whose structural invariants are maintained without any trusted party observing the network as a whole.
key_works: Distributed noninteractive zero-knowledge proofs.

title: Secret Circulation Networks — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can a secret-sharing scheme be made to move through space — its shares redistributed as the underlying network grows and reshapes — so that routing and resharing may change where information resides, yet no unauthorized coalition can ever accumulate enough compatible state to reconstruct it?
status: Dynamic proactive secret sharing addresses related concerns, but security here must additionally account for adversaries collecting shares at different places and times.
solved_when: A construction exists in which shares can be routed and reshared across a growing network, with a proof that an adversary collecting shares at different places and different times cannot assemble a reconstructing set.
why: It would enable private computation that follows available infrastructure instead of remaining tied to one fixed committee.
key_works: Dynamic proactive secret sharing.

title: Time-Expanded Cut Security — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: For a restricted linear secret-sharing protocol, is there a security certificate that bounds the information an adversary can obtain from corrupted vertices in a time-expanded transfer graph? A satisfying theorem must handle the correlated shares and adaptive corruption that arise as the graph evolves.
status: Static graph cuts are insufficient; the missing theorem must account for correlated shares and adaptive corruption. Related techniques draw on proactive sharing and distributed graph-proof methods.
solved_when: A proven bound exists on the information obtainable from corrupted vertices in the time-expanded transfer graph, accounting for correlated shares and adaptive corruption (unlike static graph-cut arguments).
why: It would give auditable secrecy guarantees for secret state that migrates, branches, and recombines across a growing network.
key_works: Proactive sharing and distributed graph-proof techniques.

title: Shape-Bound Reproduction — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can cryptographic birth of new identities in a growing network be made to respect structural constraints of the existing graph — for example bounded degree, separation from conflicting roles, or attachment only to approved neighborhoods? That is, can reproduction be shape-bound so that what is born inherits obligations from where and how it is born?
status: Currently only a proposal; no construction or proof exists. Note that logical topology is not physical geography, so any physical-location claim requires a separate attestation model. Related key works: distributed ZK graph certification and private spend prevention.
solved_when: A reproduction protocol exists in which every newly created identity provably satisfies the graph-relative constraints (bounded degree, role separation, or approved-neighborhood attachment) before admission, and structured populations cannot evade these constraints by spawning.
why: It would let autonomous populations remain organized under structural rules that hold even as the population grows, rather than being circumvented by the creation of new identities.
key_works: Distributed ZK graph certification and private spend prevention.

title: Topology-Private Development — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can a growing network develop over time so that an observer who sees only allowed outputs and leaked capacity information cannot distinguish between different development histories? Formally, construct a development protocol whose transcript distribution is indistinguishable to a specified observer across all histories consistent with the same allowed outputs and capacity leakage.
status: Currently hiding graph data does not hide network traffic, so graph-privacy techniques alone are insufficient; the proposed construction still lacks an explicit observer and communication model. Key works referenced: Path ORAM and distributed ZK certification.
solved_when: An explicit construction is given, together with a precisely specified observer and communication model, and a proof that development histories with identical allowed outputs and capacity leakage are indistinguishable to that observer.
why: It would let private coalitions and research networks expand without revealing their growth strategy to outsiders watching traffic or capacity signals.
key_works: Path ORAM and distributed ZK certification.

title: Boundary-Migrating Committees — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can a committee of nodes holding a shared cryptographic secret migrate across an administrative boundary as a single atomic step, even when the transfer of shares overlaps in time and messages are delayed or reordered? More precisely: under asynchrony, is there a protocol that simultaneously achieves share-transfer correctness and authority-transfer atomicity during migration?
status: This is a proposal; no protocol or proof exists yet. It is known that share-transfer correctness and authority-transfer atomicity are different properties and must be proved together, drawing on dynamic secret sharing and composable key-management models.
solved_when: A migration protocol is exhibited, with a proof that share-transfer correctness and authority-transfer atomicity hold together despite overlapping state transfer and delayed messages — in particular, control is never duplicated across the old and new operators.
why: It would let mobile cryptographic institutions change their operators without ever duplicating control, which is the core safety requirement for cryptographic tissues that must reassign authority while remaining live.
key_works: Dynamic secret sharing and composable key-management models.

title: Proof-Carrying Organogenesis — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can a system grow a new functional component that provably composes with everything already in place? That is, can the generated component carry a proof that it satisfies its interface contract and respects the global authority, privacy, and resource constraints of the existing system?
status: The central difficulty identified is that generated components must compose semantically; separate proofs of local correctness do not establish safe interaction. The proposal draws on proof-carrying code and universally composable security as its conceptual basis.
solved_when: A generation procedure exists whose output components come with machine-checkable certificates establishing both local interface compliance and safe composition with the existing system — not merely separate proofs of local correctness, which do not establish safe interaction.
why: It would yield infrastructure that develops genuinely new services rather than merely scaling replicas of old ones.
key_works: Proof-carrying code and universally composable security.

title: Metabolic Routing Proofs — proposal
subfield: Spatial morphogenesis: cryptographic tissues and growing networks
open: Can accepted outputs in a self-organizing processing network be made to carry a verifiable record of their processing ancestry — validation, consent, sanitization, aggregation — so that every required stage is provably present?
status: The proposed guarantee concerns authenticated protocol stages; it cannot infer unobservable physical processing from a signature alone. Key works: proof-carrying data and in-toto.
solved_when: An output is accepted only if it carries a cryptographic certificate attesting that each required protocol stage (validation, consent, sanitization, aggregation) was executed; no stage can be silently omitted.
why: It lets self-organizing processing networks enforce their obligations: participants cannot skip inconvenient processing stages without detection.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and in-toto.

title: Entitlement-Conserving Quantum Mitosis — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can scarce computational rights — entitlements to use a quantum resource — be made self-reproducing without becoming copyable? Construct a "mitosis" protocol in which a valid parent entitlement and a sufficient reproductive budget are consumed before an issuer creates the children, so that reproduction is a conserved lifecycle event rather than a cloning of an unknown quantum state.
status: The problem is at the proposal stage; issuance, surrender, and replay prevention still need a single adaptive lifecycle security proof. Related primitives include secure key leasing and certified deletion.
solved_when: A birth protocol exists with an adaptive lifecycle security proof covering issuance, surrender, and replay prevention, and demonstrating that each reproduction event consumes one valid parent entitlement plus the required reproductive budget.
why: It would let scarce computational rights multiply under explicit budgets instead of being treated as ordinary files governed by access control, which cannot enforce conservation of a quantum entitlement.
key_works: Secure key leasing and certified deletion.

title: Quantum Chrysalis Leases — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can a legitimate holder of a protected capability for a function \(f\) trade it in for a protected capability for an approved replacement \(f'\), in a way that guarantees the holder cannot still use the original capability once the new one is issued? Formally, one seeks a leasing mechanism for which unauthorized simultaneous use of both \(f\) and \(f'\) is impossible.
status: This is a proposal stage problem; no instantiation exists yet. The mechanism must be instantiated for a supported function class, since arbitrary quantum program transformation is not assumed. Related groundwork lies in secure software leasing and quantum copy-protection of restricted programs.
solved_when: A concrete instantiation of the lease-replacement mechanism is given for a specified supported function class — one not relying on arbitrary quantum program transformation — together with a proof that the holder cannot retain simultaneous use of both the old and new capabilities.
why: It would enable upgradeable protected software: licensed, copy-protected programs whose protection survives functional evolution rather than expiring or being weakened at every upgrade.
key_works: Secure software leasing and quantum copy-protection of restricted programs.

title: One-Choice Reproductive Signatures — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can we design a quantum signing token that authorizes exactly one reproductive event, in the sense that it accepts a single birth message carrying the child identities, inherited policy, and resource allocation? More formally, the token should be consumed by this one accepted use while remaining publicly verifiable as an authorization of that birth.
status: This is a proposal; no construction exists. The envisaged obstacles are that token consumption must compose with birth registration and remain sound against adversarially entangled attempts. The relevant background is quantum tokens for digital signatures.
solved_when: A quantum token scheme is constructed that (i) accepts one birth message containing child identities, inherited policy, and resource allocation, (ii) cannot be used to accept a second birth message, (iii) composes safely with birth registration, and (iv) resists adversarially entangled consumption attempts.
why: It would make scarce reproductive consent possible with publicly inspectable authorization, so third parties can verify a birth was authorized without a trusted registrar.
key_works: Quantum tokens for digital signatures.

title: Selective-Inheritance Deletion — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: After a function \(f(x)\) has been derived, can the adversarial view be pruned so that it reveals no more about \(x\) than the declared inheritance permits? Formally, deletion must leave the residual information bounded by a selective-inheritance specification.
status: This is a proposal-stage problem; no construction exists. The known constraint is that deletion must compose with prior computation and auxiliary information, and if \(f(x)\) reveals \(x\), nothing remains to protect. Related ideas come from certified deletion and everlasting-security transfer.
solved_when: A deletion procedure is exhibited that composes with the prior computation and any auxiliary information, so that whatever remains of \(x\) in the adversary's view is exactly what the inheritance declaration allows — with the caveat that if \(f(x)\) itself reveals \(x\), nothing remains to protect.
why: It would let recipients inherit the useful knowledge carried by \(f(x)\) without inheriting an unrestricted dossier about \(x\), enabling computation on data that can still be selectively forgotten afterward.
key_works: Certified deletion and everlasting-security transfer.

title: Deletion-Triggered Succession — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can we build a cryptographic capability-transfer scheme in which a successor key becomes usable only upon presentation of a valid deletion or surrender certificate for the protected predecessor capability, where the certificate is bound to the exact successor and epoch?
status: No construction is known; the proposal requires that transfers remain safe under aborted handoffs, delayed certificates, and colluding predecessor–successor pairs, in the spirit of public-key encryption with secure key leasing.
solved_when: A construction exists in which activation of the successor occurs only through a certificate as described, and the transfer provably remains safe under aborted handoffs, delayed certificates, and colluding predecessor–successor pairs.
why: It would make key handoffs establish genuine cryptographic relinquishment rather than merely contractual promises not to keep using old keys.
key_works: Public-key encryption with secure key leasing.

title: Monogamous Knowledge Lineages — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can cryptographic knowledge be made to pass down a line of delegation so that, even after many generations of descendants act on it, only a bounded number of them can ever decrypt the protected challenge — no more than the game allows?
status: The research target is recursive delegation security; ordinary uncloneability does not automatically cover arbitrary interacting descendants. Key context comes from work on uncloneable encryption and its security limitations.
solved_when: A specified challenge game is constructed in which separated descendant adversaries provably cannot exceed the allowed number of successful decryptions of the protected challenge information.
why: It would realize scarce knowledge rights that survive multiple generations of delegation, something ordinary uncloneability does not deliver.
key_works: Uncloneable encryption and its security limitations.

title: Noise-Tolerant Quantum Dormancy — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can a quantum lease — an encoded capability whose holder is restricted in how it may be used or surrendered — remain valid and recoverable over time despite noise? Formally, within a declared noise model, can the encoded lease be maintained and recovered while all surrender and use restrictions are preserved?
status: Recovery information and maintenance access can change the adversary's power; correctness under noise and leasing security have so far only been identified as needing joint analysis, drawing on secure leasing and composable certified-deletion research.
solved_when: A construction is given that, under an explicitly declared noise model, supports maintenance and recovery of the encoded lease while provably preserving its surrender and use restrictions.
why: It would enable long-lived quantum capabilities that need not remain continuously active, which is essential for cryptographic or computational resources meant to persist across idle periods.
key_works: Secure leasing and composable certified-deletion research.

title: Quantum-Share Organ Renewal — proposal
subfield: Quantum developmental cryptography
open: Can a quantum-shared secret remain secure across an evolving organ of committees — surviving specified sequences of member changes and breaches — even once the adversary has eventually encountered many historical share holders?
status: The current obstacle is that adaptive branching and recombination demand a temporal access-structure theorem that goes beyond the analysis of a single sharing episode; no such theorem is known. Related groundwork includes secret sharing with certified deletion.
solved_when: A security proof (or breaking attack) exists for sharing schemes whose access structure undergoes the specified committee-change and breach sequences, covering adversaries who accumulate historical share holders over time.
why: It would yield distributed secrets whose long-term safety does not rest entirely on unverifiable classical erasure.
key_works: Secret sharing with certified deletion.

title: Reduction-Producing Cipher Seeds — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can we automatically synthesize new cryptographic schemes — algorithms together with their security games — such that a machine-checked reduction to explicitly named hardness assumptions is produced alongside them? The core difficulty is expressive synthesis of schemes coupled with reliable automated search for valid reductions, since no generator can prove a hardness assumption true.
status: The seed cannot prove a hardness assumption true; the challenge is expressive synthesis with reliable reduction search. Related work includes EasyCrypt's mechanized cryptographic reasoning.
solved_when: The output includes generated algorithms, security games, and a machine-checked reduction to explicitly named assumptions.
why: It would enable automated cryptographic invention tailored to specialized environments, yielding schemes backed by verified reductions rather than merely plausible-looking algorithms.
key_works: EasyCrypt’s mechanized cryptographic reasoning.

title: Security-Game Germination — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can cryptographic security games be automatically generated in a way that provably preserves the security level of the games they are derived from — with each generated game linked to its inherited game by a checked implication or an explicitly labeled separation?
status: The state of the art recognizes that useful game generation requires semantic reasoning about adversarial power, not merely renaming variables and oracles; related foundations come from EasyCrypt-style verified implications and universally composable security.
solved_when: A game-generation method exists in which every generated game carries either a machine-checked implication to its inherited game or an explicitly recorded separation, so that any weakening of the advertised target is detected rather than silent.
why: It would enable protocol specifications that evolve alongside their applications, with security arguments tracked automatically as games are regenerated, instead of breaking quietly when the target is weakened.
key_works: EasyCrypt and universally composable security.

title: Assumption-Transparent Hybridization — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can a cryptographic hybrid construction carry with it a machine-checkable statement of exactly which combinations of its constituent assumptions its security depends on — whether all must hold, any single one suffices, or some more structured condition?
status: Robust combination is currently primitive-specific; concatenating two constructions does not constitute a general proof of "secure if either survives."
solved_when: A hybrid scheme is exhibited together with a checked security statement that explicitly specifies whether security requires all constituent assumptions, any one of them, or a more structured condition, and this statement remains interpretable as ingredients change.
why: It enables evolving cryptographic systems whose resilience claims stay meaningful and verifiable as their building blocks are replaced or updated.
key_works: Machine-checked cryptographic reductions and composable security.

title: Leakage-Typed Protocol Splicing — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can independently developed cryptographic components, each carrying its own formal leakage interface, be spliced into a single protocol with a machine-checkable proof that the combined leakage obeys the inherited disclosure contract?
status: The central difficulty is known: individually harmless outputs can jointly reveal a secret, so the splice checker must reason about correlation. Related definitional foundations are UC composition and functional-encryption definitions; no splicing result is currently established.
solved_when: A splicing method exists that, given components with formal leakage interfaces, verifies (or proves) that joint observations across the composed protocol stay within the disclosure contract inherited from the components — including correlation between individually harmless outputs.
why: It would enable automated construction of privacy-preserving workflows from independently developed components, which is currently unsafe because individually harmless outputs can jointly reveal a secret.
key_works: UC composition and functional-encryption definitions.

title: Private Abstraction Discovery — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can we automatically construct an abstraction of a private system that is proven to simulate the system's behavior while exposing only the intended abstract interface? Formally, the generated abstraction must satisfy a checked simulation relation and reveal only the permitted abstract interface.
status: This is a proposal-stage problem; no construction or partial results are recorded. Relevant building blocks are relational program verification and functional commitments.
solved_when: A procedure exists that, given a private system and a permitted interface, outputs an abstraction satisfying a machine-checked simulation relation, leaking nothing beyond that interface, and the abstraction is useful and non-vacuous (not merely "anything may happen").
why: It would yield inspectable guarantees for complex private systems without publishing their implementation; without non-vacuity, the guarantee is sound but worthless.
key_works: Relational program verification and functional commitments.

title: Witness-Encoding Metamorphosis — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can cryptographic proof systems be allowed to change how they encode fields, decompose bits, format numbers, and lay out witnesses — while a verified check guarantees that the semantics of the witness are preserved across the change?
status: This is a proposal; no construction or verification result exists yet. The open issue identified is that overflow, undefined behavior, and approximate arithmetic each require different preservation relations.
solved_when: Every migration of a field encoding, bit decomposition, numerical format, or witness layout is accompanied by a mechanically checked semantic-correspondence proof, with appropriate preservation relations for overflow, undefined behavior, and approximate arithmetic.
why: It would let proof systems optimize for changing hardware and workloads without numerical ambiguity becoming a security hole.
key_works: Verified compilation and updatable cryptography.

title: Parameter-Selection Autogenesis — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can a cryptographic system select and update its own security parameters — choosing key sizes, group orders, and protocol settings — in a way that provably maintains a declared concrete-security guarantee while respecting operational constraints? A solution must carry forward the underlying assumptions and estimation methods so that each update is certified, not merely plausible.
status: This is currently a proposal. No construction is known; the guiding observation is that a verified security estimate is only as sound as its attack model, so algorithmic certification cannot repair an incomplete model. Related groundwork comes from mechanized game-based security proofs.
solved_when: A parameter-update mechanism exists whose outputs satisfy an explicitly declared concrete-security model and stated operational constraints, with the assumptions and estimation methods used at each update made explicit and carried through the process.
why: It would yield adaptive cryptographic infrastructure whose security does not silently depend on undocumented or hand-tuned parameter choices, replacing ad hoc tuning with certified self-adjustment.
key_works: Mechanized game-based security proofs.

title: Cryptanalysis-Driven Primitive Evolution — proposal
subfield: Cryptography that generates cryptography
open: Can a cryptographic primitive-design system evolve under attack, so that when a break is demonstrated it records the violated security claim, retires the affected capabilities, and admits a successor only with a fresh argument covering the new design?
status: No such system exists yet; the current state is the recognition that blocking one attack does not establish security, and that any successor still requires a meaningful game and reduction or clearly stated assumption. Key works: EasyCrypt and cryptography with updates.
solved_when: A system exists that, on a demonstrated break, records the violated security claim, retires the affected capabilities, and accepts a successor primitive only with a fresh argument — a meaningful game plus reduction or a clearly stated assumption — covering its new design.
why: It would yield cryptographic infrastructure that responds systematically to demonstrated failures rather than patching ad hoc, so that blocking one attack actually feeds into a soundly argued successor rather than a false sense of security.
key_works: EasyCrypt and cryptography with updates.

title: Non-Replayable Novelty Certificates — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can a contributor prove that their artifact is genuinely new — not equivalent, under a declared equivalence relation, to anything already credited — without revealing the artifact's full contents? Formally: a proof of nonmembership in the credited set with respect to an explicitly restricted equivalence relation.
status: General semantic novelty is not efficiently decidable, so the equivalence class must be restricted and made explicit. Related building blocks exist in work on ZK accumulators and authenticated set operations.
solved_when: There exists a construction in which a prover demonstrates nonmembership of a contribution in the credited set under a declared equivalence relation, without revealing the contribution's complete contents, and the equivalence class is restricted and explicit enough for the check to be efficiently decidable.
why: It would enable open innovation markets that reward genuinely recognized new contributions rather than renamed copies of existing work.
key_works: ZK accumulators and authenticated set operations.

title: Cryptographic Heritability Trials — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can a cryptographic protocol make an evolutionary "heredity" experiment — where populations of AI agents or models reproduce, mutate, and undergo selection — verifiably honest end to end, so that skeptics can check the claimed lineage, randomness, and evaluation rather than trust the experimenter's summary?
status: This is a proposal; no protocol exists yet. The requirements are that it account for selection, missing offspring, and adaptive stopping rather than showing only successful families. Key works: Adaptive data-analysis validity and verifiable training.
solved_when: A registered parent–offspring trial exists in which the protocol cryptographically proves the prescribed randomization, mutation, evaluation, and statistical calculations over the entire enrolled sample, and correctly handles selection, missing offspring, and adaptive stopping rather than exhibiting only successful families.
why: It would yield reproducible evidence about whether agent and model improvements actually transfer to descendants, something currently impossible to establish when experimenters can curate which family lines get reported.
key_works: Adaptive data-analysis validity and verifiable training.

title: Evaluation-Exposure Genes — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Should it be possible to build a protected evaluator whose accounting of how much a lineage has been exposed to it survives the entire genealogy of that lineage — so that spawning, merging, and renaming descendants cannot reset or fragment the count? Formally: define and realize lineage-wide exposure accounting that is invariant under descendant duplication, merge, and re-identification events.
status: Currently a proposal; the requirement identified is that the accounting must include selection signals and side channels, not only explicit score queries. Related ideas include adaptive holdout reuse and privacy odometers.
solved_when: A mechanism exists in which spawning, merging, or renaming a descendant provably does not reset (or reduce) the lineage-wide exposure accounting, and the accounting includes selection signals and side channels, not only explicit score queries.
why: It would let large evolutionary searches run under meaningful limits on benchmark overfitting, instead of having those limits silently eroded through genealogical restructuring.
key_works: Adaptive holdout reuse and privacy odometers.

title: Blind Winner Propagation — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can a private selection process certify which rule won a competition and issue capabilities to its descendants, while revealing nothing beyond a prescribed selection output?
status: A proposal only. The known obstacle is that repeated winner identities and reproduction patterns can disclose rankings even when scores remain hidden; function-hiding commitments and adaptive privacy composition are the relevant starting points.
solved_when: A construction exists in which the selection output leaks at most the prescribed information — no winner identities, reproduction patterns, or rankings beyond it — even against adversaries observing repeated rounds of selection and reproduction.
why: It would let evolutionary research run competitive selection without publishing every design, protecting proprietary or sensitive candidates while still propagating winners.
key_works: Function-hiding commitments and adaptive privacy composition.

title: Anti-Self-Dealing Fitness — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can an evolutionary population's fitness be defined so that it is only earned through interactions with genuinely independent counterparties, rather than with aliases of oneself? Formally, this asks for a fitness computation built on interactions satisfying authenticated independence, challenge-generation, and contribution rules within an explicit enrolled-identity model.
status: Currently only a proposal; the key observation is that distinct credentials do not imply genuinely independent people or interests, so the enrollment assumptions must be made explicit. Related tools include ZK graph predicates and private conservation mechanisms.
solved_when: A fitness definition and evaluation mechanism exist in which fitness derives exclusively from interactions satisfying authenticated independence, challenge-generation, and contribution rules under an enrolled identity model, with the enrollment assumptions made explicit (recognizing that distinct credentials do not imply genuinely independent people or interests).
why: It would yield evolutionary service economies resistant to obvious circular self-dealing activity.
key_works: ZK graph predicates and private conservation mechanisms.

title: Proof-Bearing Niche Creation — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can an evolutionary system create a new niche only when the change is provably legitimate — that is, when each new niche refines or extends a committed task partition and carries a certificate showing how existing obligations map into the revised space?
status: Currently a proposal; the central requirement identified is that coverage measures must remain meaningful under refinement and cannot simply reward finer naming.
solved_when: A formal mechanism exists in which every niche creation event produces a machine-checkable certificate of how prior obligations map into the refined partition, and coverage measures remain meaningful under refinement rather than rewarding finer naming.
why: It enables open-ended autonomous research that can diversify without treating every change of subject as progress.
key_works: Proof-carrying data and authenticated set operations.

title: Certified Extinction Boundaries — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can a population of autonomous, self-replicating capabilities be provably shut down — where "shut down" means every active capability is retired, expired, or assigned to an explicitly limited posthumous executor — relative to a committed enrollment universe?
status: This is a proposal; the key works it builds on are ZK set operations and private spend prevention. Any proof obtained would establish extinction of recognized authority, not the disappearance of arbitrary software copies outside the system.
solved_when: A verifier can check, relative to the committed enrollment universe, that all active capabilities are retired, expired, or assigned to explicitly limited posthumous executors.
why: It enables verifiable shutdown of autonomous populations without having to publish every historical member; the proof covers extinction of recognized authority, not disappearance of arbitrary software copies outside the system.
key_works: ZK set operations and private spend prevention.

title: Mutation Contribution Shares — proposal
subfield: Evolutionary populations: selection, novelty, inheritance, extinction
open: Can mutations in a collaboratively evolving population be assigned fair, inspectable shares of credit for the final outcome? Formally, this asks for a committed attribution rule that evaluates a specified set of ablations or interventions and allocates a conserved reward across the admitted mutations.
status: Attribution is currently understood to depend on the chosen experiment and on interaction effects, so it is not an objective measure of all intellectual contribution; no committed conserved-reward allocation rule is established. Related context comes from work on verifiable training and adaptive statistical validity.
solved_when: A rule exists that, given the specified ablations or interventions, produces an allocation of the conserved reward across admitted mutations that is fully determined in advance of the experiments and whose dependence on the choice of experiment and on interaction effects is explicit and characterizable.
why: It would enable collaborative evolution with inspectable credit assignment, replacing ownership determined only by the final integrator.
key_works: Verifiable training and adaptive statistical validity.

title: Birth Before Beneficiary — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can a genesis-time commitment be made today that will later hand control to a beneficiary which does not yet exist, once that party is certified as eligible? Formally, design an activation mechanism in which the beneficiary-selection rule and inherited constraints are fixed at genesis, and a future eligible party receives control through a certified activation that resists manipulation and preserves availability without a permanent unrestricted custodian.
status: This is currently a proposal. The activation process must prevent selection manipulation and preserve availability without a permanent unrestricted custodian; candidate building blocks are functional commitments and dynamic secret sharing.
solved_when: A construction exists in which (i) the beneficiary-selection rule and all inherited constraints are committed at genesis, and (ii) a certified activation by a future eligible party grants control, with the activation process provably preventing selection manipulation and preserving availability while no permanent unrestricted custodian exists.
why: It would let endowments, scientific instruments, and services be endowed today for communities or organizations that do not yet exist, without trusting a standing custodian in the interim.
key_works: Functional commitments and dynamic secret sharing.

title: Counterfactual Descendants — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: How can a counterfactual branch of a simulation carry forward both the inherited state of its parent and a restricted set of disclosure rights, while remaining stripped of every capability for external effect? Formally, what execution model guarantees that such a branch can observe and continue its lineage but cannot act on the world?
status: Current proposals address capability attenuation and composable execution models, but the boundary remains incomplete: it must also cover indirect effects through shared services, output channels, and later incorporation of branch results.
solved_when: A composable execution and capability-attenuation model is specified under which a counterfactual descendant provably inherits simulation state and disclosure rights yet holds no external-effect capability, with the boundary covering indirect effects through shared services, output channels, and later incorporation of branch results.
why: It would let autonomous agents plan through rich simulated lineages — exploring branches and reusing their results — without risk of uncontrolled real-world reproduction of those branches' actions.
key_works: Capability attenuation and composable execution models.

title: Rejoining Timelines — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can a set of divergent timelines — each having accrued its own state, authority decisions, and external effects while apart — be merged back into a single coherent history? Formally, the question is whether a merge protocol can produce a reconciled record of state, authority, and external-effect histories while explicitly identifying the conflicts that cannot be undone.
status: Some conflicts are understood to be irreconcilable without compensation or changed guarantees; the working principle is that the protocol must expose rather than erase them. Relevant techniques include ZK set reconciliation and exactly-once effect tracking.
solved_when: A merge protocol exists that reconciles state, authority, and external-effect records across timelines and, where conflicts are irreconcilable without compensation or changed guarantees, exposes them explicitly rather than erasing them.
why: It would let offline or partitioned autonomous organizations later recover a coherent shared identity after operating independently.
key_works: ZK set reconciliation and exactly-once effect tracking.

title: Ancestral Bargains With Future Strangers — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can an ancestor commit, today, to a bounded bargaining envelope within which descendants may negotiate and execute contracts with counterparties who do not yet exist — such that no execution can ever consume more authority or resources than the ancestor originally reserved?
status: The central open tension is that the envelope must allow useful adaptation without becoming a universal authorization disguised as a template; related machinery comes from functional commitments and contextual capabilities.
solved_when: A construction exists in which future contracts are generated entirely inside the committed envelope, and their execution provably cannot spend more authority or resources than the ancestor reserved, while the envelope still permits useful adaptation rather than a universal authorization disguised as a template.
why: It would enable long-horizon coordination without requiring present parties to predict every future counterparty or circumstance.
key_works: Functional commitments and contextual capabilities.

title: Computational Seasons — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can we construct a computational primitive in which each "season" demands a prescribed sequential computation bound to a newly authenticated input, so that the guarantee is about the ordering of work rather than exact wall-clock duration?
status: Hardware variation and input withholding prevent treating sequential work as a universal physical clock. The closest known direction is verifiable delay functions.
solved_when: A construction exists in which each season's progress provably requires fresh sequential computation on a newly authenticated input, with no way to skip ahead or substitute prior seasons' work; the guarantee is on work ordering, not exact wall-clock duration.
why: It would enable developmental schedules that cannot be accelerated merely by replaying an old seed.
key_works: Verifiable delay functions.

title: Obligation-Preserving Reincarnation — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: How should a system be reincarnated so that a fresh lifetime identifier inherits only the specified unresolved duties of its predecessor while receiving no capabilities beyond those newly authorized? Formally, this asks for a mechanism in which identity continuity, liability continuity, and capability freshness are each independently guaranteed.
status: This is currently only a proposal. Related ideas include private spend prevention and proof-carrying state histories.
solved_when: A specification and construction exist in which identity continuity, liability continuity, and capability freshness are separately specified and satisfied: the new lifetime carries a fresh identifier, inherits exactly the specified unresolved obligations, and holds only newly authorized capabilities.
why: It would enable recovery and institutional revival without pretending that a dead entity's old permissions are valid again.
key_works: Private spend prevention and proof-carrying state histories.

title: Ancestry-Limited Exposure — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can a system disclose explicitly permitted lineage information about its current state while provably preventing reconstruction of earlier controllers, private states, or relationships beyond what was shared? Formalizing this "ancestry-limited exposure" requires a security game in which public outputs and retained auxiliary data across generations may already correlate, so the guarantee must hold even against an adversary that sees them.
status: This is currently a proposal. Public outputs and retained auxiliary data may already link generations, and the security game must include them; relevant tools are proactive sharing and update-hiding ZK accumulators.
solved_when: A construction and security definition exist in which all disclosure is confined to the explicitly permitted lineage information, and no adversary with access to public outputs and retained auxiliary data across generations can reconstruct non-permitted earlier controllers, private states, or relationships.
why: It would enable long-lived agents and communities whose historical privacy does not collapse under one future breach.
key_works: Proactive sharing and update-hiding ZK accumulators.

title: Commitments to Unwritten Futures — proposal
subfield: Generative time: births, branches, promises, and unwritten futures
open: Can a commitment scheme bind to a generative system — a policy, the admissible future inputs, and the rules by which they expand — so that each later opening proves the unique (or explicitly authorized) expansion of the authenticated input history? The needed primitive is adaptive binding and hiding for expanding object graphs, not ordinary commitment to a fixed string.
status: The missing foundation is adaptive binding and hiding for expanding object graphs — not ordinary commitment to a fixed string; related lines include functional commitments, proof-carrying data, and cryptography with updates.
solved_when: A commitment scheme exists for which genesis commits to a generative policy, admissible future inputs, and expansion rules, and every later opening proves the unique or explicitly authorized expansion for the authenticated input history, with adaptive binding and hiding over the expanding object graph.
why: It would enable open-ended cryptographic worlds whose inhabitants, rules, and artifacts emerge over time while remaining accountable to their origin.
key_works: Functional commitments, proof-carrying data, and cryptography with updates.
